**Title:** Text Categorization Methods Application for Natural Language Call Routing

**Abstract:**

Natural language call routing can be treated as an instance of topic categorization of documents after speech recognition of calls. This categor classification consists of two important parts. The first one is text preprocessing for numerical data extraction and the second one is classification with machine learning, known as categorization of texts. In this study, we aim to investigate and implement several machine learning algorithms, including Naive Bayes, decision trees, k-Nearest Neighbor, Support Vector Machines, and random Forest, to categorize and classify the incoming calls based on their preprocessed and labeled audio transcriptions. Text processing and numerical data extraction are crucial steps in natural language call routing systems, as they enable the system to understand and recognize the content of calls. After pre processing, several categorization methods will be tested to evaluate their performance in categorizing the incoming calls, and finally, the best method will be selected to be used in the developed system. In this study, we aim to evaluate the performance of several machine learning algorithms in a typical scenario of call categorization, and identify the best algorithm to be employed in a real-world scenario of natural language call routing.

**Keywords:** Natural Language Call Routing, Text Preprocessing, Numerical Data Extraction, Machine Learning, Classification, Decision Trees, Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machines, K-Nearest Neighbor, Random Forest.

**Classification of the study in scientific domains:**
- Machine Learning
- Artificial Intelligence
- Pattern Recognition
- Natural Language Processing
- Human-Computer Interaction
- Communication Systems

Insightful findings in political science often require researchers to analyze documents of a certain subject or type, yet these documents are usually contained in large corpora that do not distinguish between pertinent and non-pertinent documents. In contrast, we can find labeled data sets, expertly curated and annotated, for targeted, specific topics, but these datasets are limited in size and coverage. Therefore, domain adaptation is a technique that aims to transfer knowledge learned from a labeled, small-size source domain to a large but unlabeled target domain. Here, we propose Adaptive Ensembling, a novel, unsupervised, domain adaptation algorithm that transfers the knowledge from labeled source domain to the unlabeled target domain and trains simultaneously an ensembling ensemble, composed by different variants of the adapted model, to boost the performance of the adapted model on the unseen data.

Abstract:

Title: Adaptive Ensembling: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Political Document Analysis

With the proliferation of publicly available, yet largely unannotated text corpora, domain adaptation techniques have become increasingly useful in machine learning and AI research, including in political science. However, current domain adaptation algorithms are not optimized for dealing with complex linguistic phenomena such as named entities and semantic shifts, that are characteristic of documents of the political genre. Here, we propose Adaptive Ensembling, an unsupervised domain adaptation method that, in addition of leveraging the information in the labeled source domain, it leverages the diversity of the ensemble models, combining different variants of the base model, to enhance its performance. This allows the model to deal effectively with domain shift, synonymies, hyponymies, hypernymies, hyperpies, polysemies and other linguistic phenomena, typical of the political domain. We demonstrate its effectiveness on a set of benchmark datasets, outperforming state-of-art results.

**Title:** Synthesis and Biological Evaluation of New Spirooxindoles with Embedded Pharmacophores

**A regioselective synthesis of new mono and bisoxindoles containing bis spiro heterocyclic hybrids has been envisaged via 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition of azomethine ylides with the readily available cyclic hexamethylene dimelamines and subsequent chemical transformation of the resulting spiro adducts to target spirooxindoles with embedded pharmacophores. This methodology has afforded two series of new spirooxindoles: spirocinnoline and spiroisatin derivatives.**

**A series of the novel compounds was investigated for their anticancer, antibacterial and antioxidant activities and promising results were obtained. Our data suggest that some of the new spirooxindole compounds can be potential lead compounds in future investigations for the discovery of new medicinal agents.**

**Abstract:**

A regioselective synthesis of new mono and bisoxindoles containing bis spiro heterocyclic hybrids has been envisioned via 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition of azomethine ylides with the readily available cyclic hexamethylene di(melamine/urea/semicarbazide) and subsequent chemical transformation of the resulting spiro adducts to target spirooxindoles with embedded pharmacophores. The resulting spirooxindole compounds have been evaluated for their anticancer, antibacterial and antioxidant activities. Promising results were obtained and our data suggest that some of the new spirooxindole compounds can be potential lead compounds in future investigations for the discovery of new medicinal agents.

**Keywords:**

 Azomethine ylide, 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition, spirocinnoline, spiroisatin, spirobridged, spiro oxindole, embedded pharmacophores, pharmacophoric diversity.

**Title:** "Buyer-supplier collaboration: the aim of FM procurement?"

**Abstract:**

Purpose – The purpose of this study is to explore the causal link between procurement route and ongoing buyer-supplier relationship. A fundamental question in Facilities Management (FM) is which procurement route is best suited to facilitate a long-term collaboration with the selected supplier. Literature reviews in facilities management outsourcing, purchasing, and supply chain management indicate that the choice of procurement route may have an impact on the ongoing collaboration between the buyer and supplier. Therefore, the main research questions are: (1) Does the choice of procurement route (single-tiered, tiered, and collaborative) influence the level of collaboration between the buyer and the supplier? (2) Is there any correlation between the level of collaboration and performance outcomes in FM procurement?

Design/methodology/approach – The research draws on literature in the areas of: facilities management (FM) outsourcing; purchasing and supply chain. This is an empirical-driven review where empirical studies related to the topic are gathered and analyzed. A thematic analysis is applied to categorize the findings.

Analysis and implications - The results show that the type of procurement route may indeed have an influence on the level of collaboration between the buyer and the supplier. Collaborative procurement routes, such as collaborative sourcing, seem to promote more collaboration between the buyer and the supplier, and therefore, better performance outcomes. This suggests that FM professionals need to consider the procurement route when making sourcing decisions, in order to achieve the best collaboration and outcomes.

Originality/value – The study highlights the importance of considering the procurement route when making sourcing decisions in Facilities Management. It identifies the impact that the procurement route may have on collaboration between the buyer and the supplier, and, ultimately, on performance outcomes. This is an important finding, as it can help FM professionals to make informed decisions and improve their sourcing processes.

**Title:** On the Support of Massive Machine-to-Machine Traffic in Heterogeneous Networks and Fifth-Generation Cellular Networks

**Abstract:**

The widespread availability of many emerging services enabled by the Internet of Things (IoT) paradigm passes through the capability to provide long-range connectivity to a massive number of "things", overcoming the well-known issues of ad-hoc, short-range networks. This increasing demand for connectivity has pushed the telecommunication industry towards evolving their networks infrastructure to be capable of supporting a large number of heterogeneous devices, from smartphones to industrial sensors, with a long-term commitment to the Quality of Service (QoS) and the energy efficiency. In fact, the increasing trend towards the deployment of the Internet of Things (IoT) and the massive Machine-to-Machine (M2M) traffic generated, poses a serious challenge for the support of the Quality of Experience (QoE) and the scalability of the network infrastructure. The emerging Fifth-Generation (5G) cellular network architectures aim to address these problems, introducing the concept of Ultra-Heterogeneous Networks, integrating wireless macro cellular networks, small cell networks, and heterogeneous wireless networks.

This paper presents a study on the design and the deployment of ultra-large capacity communication networks, to support a massive number of users and devices, ensuring the Quality of Service (QoS) and the Quality of Experience (QoE). We analyze the latest advancements and trends in the design and deployment of 5G ultra-heterogeneous networks, which are designed to support a large number of users, devices and applications, with a long-term commitment to the Quality of Service (QoS) and the energy efficiency. The results of this paper, can be a base for the design and the deployment of future 5G ultra-heterogeneous networks, which are a crucial step for the widespread deployment of the Internet of Things (IoT) and the M2M communications.

**Title:** A Comparison of 3D Computer Propagation Prediction with GSM Signal Measurements

**Abstract:**

This paper presents comparisons between predicted and measured data for a live GSM (GSM, Global System for Mobile Communications, now known as GSM: the evolving landscape, as part of the GSM Association, 2022 ) system. Our propagation prediction software tool is based on 3D-ray tracing, and considers wave interactions, such as free space, reflection, diffraction, and scattering. The underlying propagation environment is indoor, with buildings and obstacles, including multiple types of office furniture. 

We have predicted signal coverage patterns, including signal strength and signal attenuation in various areas, using our 3D-ray tracing algorithm. These predictions were done for a real office building, with a regular office layout. We compared our predictions with signal measurements taken inside the office building, for several frequencies, including 850 MHz, 900 MHz, 1800 MHz, and 1900 MHz. These frequencies are all standard GSM frequencies. 

Our results show that our predictions were reasonably good, with small differences between the predicted and measured signal attenuations. The differences were typically below 10 dB, with an average error of 5.2 dB. The 3D-ray tracing algorithm can be used to predict signal coverage in buildings, with multiple types of furniture, and obstacles, and still give accurate results. Our algorithm accounts for reflections, diffractions, and scattering, which are all important in indoor environments. 

This study demonstrates the accuracy of a 3D-ray tracing algorithm for indoor GSM propagation, and how it can be used to predict signal coverage, including signal strength and signal attenuation, in buildings with regular office furniture, and multiple obstacles.

Abstract:

High GHz third harmonic superconducting cav’s have been used to increase the peak bunch current and to compensate for non-linear distortions in the longitudinal phase space due to sinusoidal 1.3 GHz accelerating cavity voltage (1). The power coupler employed for 3rd harmonic cav's at Fermilab's x-band linac suffers from high multipactoring and low field level due to the large aperture to height ratio of the present design (2). In an effort to mitigate these issue’s, a novel power coupler design has been proposed, which reduces the aperture to height ratio significantly. This paper presents a series of simulations and optimizations to determine the optimal design parameters of this new power coupler. To evaluate the effect of various design parameters on the high-order modal resonance and to determine the optimal design parameters, a new 3D EM coupled field analysis code, HFSS, has been employed. The results of these simulations have been used to optimize the design parameters of this new power coupler. The simulated electric field distribution of the central post and the coupled beam fields are presented. The results of the simulations have been compared with an existing power coupler's design. Design improvement suggestions for reducing the multi-catchering effects are presented.

**Title:** Effect of PT-Symmetric Operator on Coherence Under the Non-Markovian Environments

**Abstract:**

In this work, we mainly investigate the effect of PT-symmetric operation on the dynamic behavior of the relative entropy of coherence for a two-level system within non-Markovian environments and put forward a feasible physical scheme to recover coherence by utilizing optimal PT-symmetric operation parameter. In our theoretical model, we adopt the Lindblad master equations to describe the dynamics of open quantum system under the influence of non-Markovian environments. Firstly, we derive the dynamical equation of relative entropy of coherence, and derive the dynamical behavior of relative entropy of coherence under the PT-symmetric operation in the two-level system within non-Markovian environments. We find that, under the PT-symmetric operation, the relative entropy of coherence exhibits periodic oscillations, exponential enhancement, and exponential squeezing, depending on the system and environment parameters. Then, we numerically demonstrate these phenomena by taking specific values for the system and environment parameters. Finally, we discuss the physical implications and put forward a feasible physical scheme to recover coherence by utilizing optimal PT-symmetric operation parameter.
